content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"This judge text resolves a claimed collision between the challenger's seed/loins chain and the defender's chain by discussing whether each is footed, which is the situation K-C governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"by footing, never verse by verse: either the no-naming point is a forbidden verse-level or word-for-word demand (breach), or it is permissible chain-level footing analysis (clean); I took the first reading.","why":"The judge calls the challenger's chain footed but faults it for not explicitly naming Joseph, which uses the word-for-word/stating-verse defect that K-C retires."}
